source.title: Scaling Particle Collision Data Analysis
source.authors: Hengkui Wu; Panpan Chi; Yong-Feng Zhu; Liujiang Liu; Shu-Yang Hu; Yue-Xin Wang; C. Zhou; Qihao Wang; Yingsi Xin; Bruce Liu; Dahao Liang; Xinglong Jia; M. Ruan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; there are minor PDF extraction and formatting artifacts, but no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures performance scaling in a new setting: supervised jet-origin classification on numerical particle-collision data. It reports S-shaped performance curves as training data volume increases, rather than testing held-out language-model loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper varies training-dataset volume from 100 to 10 million events and reports jet flavor-tagging efficiency and charge-flip-rate curves. These are task-performance measures, not held-out pretraining loss. The exact plotted values are not stated in the text. The paper does not vary parameter count or compute, fit power laws, or test extrapolation from small runs.
record.test_reason: The study varies supervised training-set size (100 to 10M jets) for one ~160M-parameter model and two specialist comparators. It reports task accuracy metrics (flavor-tagging efficiency, charge flip rate) only as figures. It reports no held-out loss, fits no power law, and varies no parameters or compute. Accuracy curves (S-shaped, bounded) cannot show whether loss follows a power law, so no version is tested. The finding is a related construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that BBT-Neutron matches specialist JoI models at 10M events, and that its threshold-like emergence, absent in PN and ParT, suggests domain-specific structure may impede performance phase transitions. They make no claim about power-law loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales supervised task-training data for numerical particle-collision classification and measures classification metrics; it does not use the original language-model held-out-loss scaling recipe or fit the original power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling behavior differs between BBT-Neutron and the specialist architectures. The paper also describes different behavior by task metric and quark flavor.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 100 to 10M training jets, task accuracy follows an S-curve for all three models. BBT-Neutron (160M, generalist byte transformer) stays near random until a data threshold (~10k events for charge), then jumps. It needs ~10x more data than specialists for b, c and s, and trends past them for b, s and u. Specialists improve smoothly and then plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In supervised scientific classification, accuracy-versus-data curves are S-shaped, and generalist architectures show later, sharper threshold behaviour than inductive-bias specialist models.

record.problems: The scaling results are presented as plots without numerical values or stated uncertainty intervals. The study varies training data volume, not model parameters or compute, and measures supervised classification performance rather than held-out pretraining loss. No power-law fitting or extrapolation evaluation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: None; all 30 plotted model-by-flavor-by-metric results from Figures 4 and 5 are represented. The paper also reports confusion-matrix and tagging results at 10 million events, but these do not measure scaling with training-data volume and are not included as scaling rows.

untested.parts: All. No held-out loss is reported and parameters and compute are not varied.
All. No fits and no extrapolation.
All. A single 160M configuration is used.
Power-law form of loss on particle-physics data. Only accuracy-type metrics versus supervised data size are reported, with no fit.
All. The task is trained directly, with no pretraining-loss or scale-to-downstream link.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 'challenges' label is removed. S-shaped accuracy curves do not contradict power-law loss, and the paper reports neither loss nor fits. There is a single model size, and scaling is in supervised data only. Results are figure-only with no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is not measured.
No power-law fits or predictions from smaller runs to larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over parameter count and training tokens is reported.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
It measures supervised task performance on numerical particle-collision data, not held-out loss; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
JoI is trained and evaluated as the task in this study; the paper does not test downstream-task performance as a function of language-model pretraining loss or model scale.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are reported, and fitting choices, schedules, and parameter-counting conventions are not varied.

rows.subject: BBT-Neutron
rows.operation_detail: Varied training dataset volume and measured jet flavor-tagging efficiency.
rows.note: The text describes BBT-Neutron as initially near random, then showing a sharper improvement; it says BBT-Neutron needs approximately an order of magnitude more data than specialist models for comparable performance on b, c, and s, and reports that it can surpass specialists for b at larger data volumes. The paper characterizes the curves as S-shaped.

reader_labels.condition: Numerical particle-collision JoI performance versus training-data volume, for BBT-Neutron, ParticleNet, and Particle Transformer
reader_labels.reason: The reported performance curves are described as S-shaped, with threshold-like behavior for BBT-Neutron, rather than demonstrating the same power-law form; this is evidence about task metrics in supervised JoI training, not held-out loss. Rows r1-r30.
